svg.title: Figure 4. Thin-wall and thick-wall hoop stress
svg.desc: Two panels. (a) Hoop and radial stress divided by the pressure across the wall of the lab tube: the Lame hoop stress falls from about 5.5 at the inner surface to about 4.5 at the outer surface, the radial stress rises from minus 1 to zero, and the thin-wall value p r_i/t is a horizontal line at 5.0, equal to the average of the hoop stress; an open circle marks the outer surface, where the gages are. (b) The relative error of p r_i/t against the radius ratio r_o/r_i from 1 to 2: compared with the Lame value at the outer surface the thin-wall formula is high by half of (r_o/r_i minus 1), 10 percent for the lab tube; compared with the inner surface it is low; a shaded band marks errors above 5 percent.
